tasks.title: Go module skeleton: command tree, global flags, exit codes, version, embedded plugin
tasks.goal: Everything later in the run hangs off this: the `github.com/mvelosop/vloop` module, a cobra command tree whose global flags and 0/1/2 exit-code mapping every later command inherits, `vloop version`, and the plugin skeleton embedded into the binary. The embed is the trap the design names — without the `all:` prefix `plugin/.claude-plugin/` is silently dropped and everything else still builds — so the binary must read the plugin version from its embedded copy, never from the working tree. Build no other command.

references.why: Behaviour contract: 'The binary and its global surface', 'vloop version' and 'The embedded plugin' — flags, exit codes, stderr format, version text and JSON key order

Section 2 fixes the layout this task creates: root embed.go in package vloop with the all: prefix, cmd/vloop, internal/cli, plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (ignore its schemas/ directory — that is B2)

acceptance: go.mod declares module `github.com/mvelosop/vloop` with a `go` line for the current stable release; the only third-party dependency added is cobra.
`go build -o <out>/vloop ./cmd/vloop` builds a binary named vloop.

`vloop version` prints exactly `vloop <version> (commit <commit>, plugin <plugin>, <go> <os>/<arch>)`; `vloop version --json` prints one JSON object with keys `version, commit, plugin, go, os, arch` in that order; go/os/arch are `runtime.Version()`, `runtime.GOOS`, `runtime.GOARCH`.
`version` and `commit` are package-level variables `main.version` and `main.commit` in cmd/vloop, defaulting to `0.0.0-dev` and `unknown`, overridable with `-ldflags -X`.

`plugin` is read at runtime from the embedded plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (via a root `embed.go` using `//go:embed all:plugin`), never from the working tree — a violation is any os.ReadFile/os.Open of plugin.json.

plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json has name `vloop` and version `0.0.0-dev`; .claude-plugin/marketplace.json has name `vloop` and exactly one plugin `{"name":"vloop","source":"./plugin"}`. No skills, agents, hooks or schemas/ are created.

A committed test in the root package proves the embedded FS contains `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (it would fail without the `all:` prefix); a committed test in internal/cli runs `version --json` and checks every field.
Global persistent flags on every command: `-C/--dir`, `--json`, `--no-color`, `-q/--quiet`, `-v/--verbose`; a non-empty `NO_COLOR` disables colour; colour only when stdout is a terminal.

Unknown command, unknown flag or missing argument exits 2 with exactly one stderr line starting `vloop: ` and nothing on stdout, with or without `--json` (cobra's usage dump is silenced). The mapping has a distinct path for exit 1 (command ran and found problems) that later commands use.
No other command (config, brief, task, status, init, doctor, run) is added in this task.
No product code or test reads or writes this repo's `.loop/` or `.claude/`, or the home directory; tests work in `t.TempDir()` scratch repos.
`gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, and the module builds for linux, windows and the host.

tasks.title: Repo root resolution and `vloop config get|set|list|path`
tasks.goal: Every later command needs the repo root and the configured language, and later briefs read model and effort per session kind from here. This task adds root discovery (nearest `.vloop`, else nearest `.git`, else the start dir) and a repo-local `.vloop/config.toml` with env overrides, implementing every row of the brief's key table. Config is repo-local only — nothing global — and per-task overrides are B2, not here.

references.why: 'The repo root' and 'vloop config get | set | list | path': the key table, resolution order, output formats, exact error messages and exit codes, byte-for-byte idempotent set
'Decisions every brief inherits': config lives only in .vloop/config.toml plus VLOOP_* variables; nothing read from or written to a global location

acceptance: Repo root: nearest ancestor of the -C dir (or cwd) containing `.vloop`, else nearest containing `.git`, else the start dir; all printed paths are root-relative with `/` separators on every OS.

Keys in order language, model.plan, model.work, model.review, effort.plan, effort.work, effort.review with the brief's defaults and valid values; resolution env (`VLOOP_` + upper-cased key with `.`→`_`) over file over default.
`config list` prints `<key>=<value> (<source>)` per key, unset effort as `effort.plan= (default)`; `--json` is an object in key order of `{value, source}` with unset as null.
`config get <key>` prints the value and a newline (empty line for unset effort); `--json` prints `{key, value, source}` in that order.

`config set` validates, creates .vloop/config.toml under the root if absent, preserves every other key, prints nothing on success, leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged when the value is already set, and `set <key> ''` removes the key.
`config path` prints `.vloop/config.toml` whether or not it exists and creates nothing.

Unknown key: `vloop: unknown config key "<key>"`, exit 2. Invalid value: `vloop: invalid value "<value>" for <key>: want one of <a>, <b>, …` (models: `want a non-empty string`), exit 2, file untouched.

An invalid value from the environment or the file, or a malformed TOML file, exits 1 with one `vloop: ` stderr line naming the source (the variable name, or the config file path); under `--json` stdout still carries exactly one JSON document.
One TOML library is the only new dependency; nothing reads `~/.config` or any global path.
Committed tests cover every key-table row, env/file/default resolution, idempotent set, removal, the exit-2 cases and all three root-resolution branches, in temporary directories.
No product code or test reads or writes this repo's `.loop/` or `.claude/`, or the home directory; tests work in `t.TempDir()` scratch repos.
`gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, and the module builds for linux, windows and the host.

tasks.title: Brief parsing and the English `vloop brief check` (port of check-brief.sh)
tasks.goal: `brief check` is how an operator knows a brief is fit to plan; this task ports every rule of the shell checker to Go against the English heading set, with the same problem/warning split and wording, and wires the command's text and JSON output. The plannable marker is now frontmatter `status: ready` (the body `**Status:**` line is gone), and journals live under `.vloop/state/journals/`. Frontmatter validity, binding-reference, Spanish and depends-on rules are later tasks — but structure the heading set as data so T4 can add Spanish without rewriting rules.

references.why: the rules being ported — regexes, problem vs warning split, message wording and the skip logic; port the rules, not the shell, and swap .loop/state/journals/ for .vloop/state/journals/
'The vloop brief format' and 'vloop brief check <path>…': heading matching, output markers and summary lines, the JSON shape, the no-such-brief and not-a-loop-brief cases and their exit codes
Section 4: brief check validates the brief as vloop's only public contract; nothing upstream of a loop brief is recognised

acceptance: Every rule of `.loop/check-brief.sh` is ported with the same problem/warning split and the same message wording (without ANSI colour): already run (journal at `.vloop/state/journals/<run id>.md`, run id = name minus `.loop-brief`), worked example, fenced block, out-of-scope section and item count, constraints, task count, exit/status codes, absolute home path (macOS, Linux and a Windows user-profile path: drive letter, colon, backslash, `Users`), more than two pinned symbols, unresolved backticked path outside `## Binding references` (resolved as the shell does: repo root, brief dir, or a file of that basename in the repo), tracker keys and tracker URLs.
Only briefs with frontmatter `status: ready` are checked; others print their path and `- skipped: status is <status>`.
Headings match the configured language's heading set, case-insensitively, with trailing text allowed; the English set is product data in a non-test file.

Output per brief: root-relative path, one line per rule with `✓`/`!`/`✗`, then `ok, <n> warning(s)` or `<n> problem(s), <m> warning(s)`; final line `briefs ok` or `<n> brief(s) need work`. Exit 0 iff no brief has problems.

A missing path prints `vloop: no such brief: <path>` on stderr and counts as needing work; a path not ending in `.loop-brief.md` is `vloop: not a loop brief: <path>`, exit 2, before any brief is checked; no path at all is exit 2.
`--json` prints exactly one document `{"ok":bool,"briefs":[{"path","result":"ok|problems|skipped","problems":[…],"warnings":[…]}]}` (messages without the marker), on exit 0 and exit 1.
Committed fixtures: for every ported rule, a brief where it passes and one where it fires, exercised by committed tests in temporary scratch repos.
Tests never read `.loop/check-brief.sh` or anything else under `.loop/`; the port is Go code, not a shell-out.
`gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, and the module builds for linux, windows and the host.

tasks.title: Frontmatter validity and `## Binding references` rules
tasks.goal: The brief is vloop's only public contract, and its binding references are now the only way a document binds a task (there is no loop-knowledge scan), so `brief check` must prove each one resolves and says why it binds. It must also refuse a brief whose frontmatter is broken or whose name disagrees with its filename, whatever its status. Both languages' section headings apply.

references.why: 'New rules' — Frontmatter and Binding references — with their exact messages, which apply to every brief ready or not, and the entry format: backticked path, then ` — ` or ` - `, then a non-empty reason

Both ` — ` and ` - ` separators are accepted.

tasks.title: `depends-on`: resolution, cycles, and `vloop brief list`
tasks.goal: Briefs declare their predecessors so the series (B1→B2→B3→B4) has an order vloop can show and enforce. This task resolves `depends-on` names against the loop briefs in docs/briefs/, reports dangling names and cycles in `brief check`, and adds `brief list` in dependency order with a ready/blocked column. Only `*.loop-brief.md` files exist as far as vloop is concerned.

references.why: 'Dependencies' rules with exact messages, 'vloop brief list' output and JSON shape, and the worked example's list and cycle lines

acceptance: A `depends-on` name with no loop brief in docs/briefs/ is the problem `depends-on does not resolve: <name>` (a name matching a non-loop-brief file does not resolve).
A cycle is the problem `depends-on cycle: <a> -> <b> -> <a>`, starting from the checked brief.

`brief list` prints `<name>  <status>  <ready>  <depends-on>` (two-space separated, no padding) for every loop brief, in dependency order with ties broken by name (a brief is listed as soon as its dependencies are, lowest name first); `<ready>` is `-` for a consumed brief, `ready` when every dependency is consumed (including none), else `blocked`; `<depends-on>` is the names joined by `,` or `-`.
`brief list --json` is an array of `{name, path, status, ready, depends_on}` in that key order, `depends_on` an array.
A cycle or dangling dependency makes `brief list` exit 1 with the same message on stderr (prefixed `vloop: `) and nothing on stdout.
Files in docs/briefs/ not named `*.loop-brief.md` are invisible to list and check.
Committed tests cover resolution, dangling names, cycles, ordering and the ready column.
`gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, and the module builds for linux, windows and the host.
